parts.text: Which sequence correctly produces lightning and thunder?

options.text: Rubbing separates charges; a large buildup breaks down the insulating property of air; a sudden discharge is lightning; rapid heating of air makes thunder.
Thunder is produced first; the sound then separates the charges and forms lightning.
Rubbing separates charges and lightning flashes even when the buildup is too small to break down the insulating property of air.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: After cricket practice, Siddharth sees a bright flash from a storm cloud and soon hears thunder. Strong upward and downward winds in the cloud make water droplets and ice particles rub against each other.

part_answers.answer: Charge separation from rubbing must build up enough to break down air before a discharge (lightning); thunder follows from the rapid heating and expansion of air, so thunder cannot come first.

teacher.key_rationale: Rubbing charges particles; only a large enough buildup breaks down air to give lightning; thunder follows from rapid heating of air. Reversing thunder first or dropping the buildup condition is wrong.
